prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the layered 3D geometry of an indoor climbing gym where the camera wearer stands in a tight huddle of about six to eight people within 0.2 to 2.0 metres, with an overhanging climbing wall 2 to 5 metres to the upper right and an elevated mezzanine 5 to 8 metres away in the upper-left background. Across frames 1 to 3, the brightest white region on the right edge shows a person's head within 0.2 to 0.4 metres—well within arm's reach and partly cropped by the right frame border—while a person in a teal shirt stands 0.5 to 0.8 metres in front and slightly left (turning from facing away-left in frame 1 to facing right in frame 2 as they approach closer in frame 3), with others in red, grey, and dark shirts arranged 1.0 to 1.8 metres away in a semicircle facing inward and not looking at the camera wearer. In frames 4 and 5, the camera pitches upward and turns slightly right, causing the huddle to drop out of the lower frame except for the bright top of a nearby head (0.3 to 0.5 metres below/in front) while the sloped plane of the climbing wall on the right and the distant ceiling/balcony on the left become prominent. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground overlapping arms (0.4 to 0.9 metres, within everyone's reach) from the torso of the teal-shirted person and reveals the continuous planar slope of the overhanging climbing wall despite its visually busy holds. However, the depth map is unreliable on the distant mezzanine railing and ceiling trusses where fine structures merge into uniform black, and in frame 3 where the foreground reaching arm and the teal shirt blend into a nearly identical mid-grey depth value despite one occluding the other.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map partitions the foreground huddle into individual 'person' masks, isolating six to eight closely packed people located 0.2 to 2.0 metres from the camera wearer and less than 0.5 metres from one another, while leaving the background climbing wall and mezzanine unsegmented black. In frames 1 to 3, distinct masks delineate the partially visible person on the extreme right edge (0.2 to 0.4 metres away, facing left), the central-left person in the teal shirt (0.5 to 0.8 metres away, occluding the middle-ground group), and the semicircle of people behind and to the left and right (1.0 to 1.8 metres away, facing the center of the circle rather than the camera wearer) whose outstretched arms overlap within arm's reach at the bottom center. As the camera tilts upward in frames 4 and 5, only the top of the closest person's head at the bottom center-right (0.3 to 0.5 metres) and three partially cropped heads at the bottom left (1.0 to 1.5 metres) receive 'person' masks, while a person standing on the distant upper-left balcony (6 to 8 metres above and left) is misclassified as a 'bottle'. This map makes it easier than RGB to count distinct individuals and trace boundary contours in the cluttered, overlapping crowd in frames 1 and 2. However, it is unreliable where overlapping arms in frames 1 to 3 are either merged into adjacent torso masks (such as the foreground arm absorbed into the pink mask of the teal-shirted person in frame 3) or dropped entirely, and where the distant person on the balcony in frames 4 and 5 is falsely labeled 'bottle' while the adjacent head on the lower right of frame 4 is missed.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, detecting only a single partial upper-body skeleton (yellow) and two hand skeletons (magenta) on the left side of frame 1, and a single isolated hand skeleton on the far left of frame 2, all between 0.8 and 1.5 metres from the camera wearer. In frame 1, the yellow torso and arm keypoints belong to a person in the left-center background (about 1.2 metres away, facing right/inward with an arm extended forward to the left), terminating near two overlapping magenta hand skeletons at the lower-left edge that are within arm's reach of the people on the left side of the huddle. In frame 2, only one magenta hand skeleton remains visible on the left edge at roughly 1.0 metre distance, and in frames 3, 4, and 5—as the foreground people move closer and the camera subsequently tilts upward toward the climbing wall—no body or hand keypoints are detected at all. Where present in frames 1 and 2, the magenta keypoints help localize the articulated finger positions of the overlapping hands in the lower-left tangle, which are partially occluded and hard to parse in the RGB image. However, the map is highly unreliable throughout the sequence because severe mutual occlusion, close-range cropping of bodies at 0.2 to 0.8 metres, and top-down head views in frames 4 and 5 cause the pose estimator to miss nearly all people and outstretched arms in the scene.
